events.title: The First Battery
events.body: Alessandro Volta describes his 'pile' — discs of zinc and copper separated by brine-soaked card — the first source of steady electric current.

events.title: The White House Occupied
events.body: President John Adams moves into the still-unfinished President's House in the new capital, Washington. It was built partly by enslaved labourers.

events.title: The United Kingdom Is Formed
events.body: The Act of Union joins Great Britain and Ireland into one United Kingdom, with one parliament in London.

events.title: Ceres Discovered
events.body: On New Year's night, Giuseppe Piazzi in Palermo spots a moving point of light: Ceres, the first object found in the belt between Mars and Jupiter.

events.title: Ranjit Singh Crowned
events.body: Ranjit Singh is proclaimed Maharaja of the Punjab. From Lahore he builds a Sikh empire that holds off the British until after his death.

events.title: The Cane Ridge Revival
events.body: Thousands gather for days of open-air preaching in Kentucky, a high point of the Second Great Awakening that reshapes American religion.

events.title: Gia Long Unites Vietnam
events.body: Nguyễn Ánh defeats his rivals and proclaims himself Emperor Gia Long, ruling a united Vietnam from Huế.

events.title: The Louisiana Purchase
events.body: Napoleon sells France's vast Louisiana territory to the United States, doubling its size — land on which many Native nations already lived.

events.title: The Saudis Take Mecca
events.body: Forces of the first Saudi state, allied with the strict reform movement of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, take Mecca from Ottoman control.

events.title: Haiti Becomes Independent
events.body: After the only successful slave revolution in history, Jean-Jacques Dessalines declares independence. Haiti becomes the first free Black republic and the second independent country in the Americas.

events.title: The First Railway Locomotive
events.body: Richard Trevithick's steam engine hauls iron and passengers along a tramway in south Wales — the first locomotive to run on rails.

events.title: The Castle Hill Rebellion
events.body: Hundreds of convicts, many of them Irish rebels, rise near Sydney. Soldiers crush them within a day.

events.title: The Napoleonic Code
events.body: France adopts a single civil code. Its rules on property, contracts and the family are copied across Europe and Latin America.

events.title: Lewis and Clark Set Out
events.body: Meriwether Lewis and William Clark lead an expedition from St. Louis to the Pacific and back. Sacagawea, a Shoshone woman, guides and interprets for part of the way.

events.title: The Sokoto Jihad
events.body: Usman dan Fodio, a Fulani scholar, leads a reform movement against the Hausa kings. The Sokoto Caliphate becomes one of the largest states in 19th-century Africa.

events.title: Napoleon Crowns Himself
events.body: In Notre-Dame, with the Pope looking on, Napoleon takes the crown and places it on his own head.

events.title: Muhammad Ali Takes Egypt
events.body: An Albanian officer in the Ottoman army becomes governor of Egypt. He builds a modern army, factories and canals, and his family rules Egypt until 1952.

events.title: Trafalgar
events.body: Nelson's fleet destroys the combined French and Spanish fleets off Spain. Nelson is killed, but Britain rules the seas for a century.

events.title: Austerlitz
events.body: On the anniversary of his coronation, Napoleon crushes the armies of Russia and Austria in Moravia — his most celebrated victory.

events.title: Britain Takes the Cape
events.body: British forces defeat the Dutch garrison at Blaauwberg, north of Cape Town. The Cape becomes a British colony.

events.title: The British Take Buenos Aires
events.body: A British force captures Buenos Aires. Local militias drive it out within weeks, and defeat a second invasion in 1807 — a confidence that feeds the push for independence.

events.title: The Holy Roman Empire Ends
events.body: Under pressure from Napoleon, Francis II gives up the crown of the thousand-year-old Holy Roman Empire.

events.title: The Slave Trade Abolished
events.body: Britain's Slave Trade Act bans British ships from carrying enslaved Africans. Slavery itself stays legal in the colonies for another generation.

events.title: Sierra Leone Becomes a Crown Colony
events.body: Freetown, settled by Black Loyalists from America and by freed Africans, becomes a British colony — and the port where the navy lands Africans freed from slave ships.

events.title: The Dos de Mayo Uprising
events.body: The people of Madrid rise against the French occupation. The next day French troops shoot hundreds of prisoners. Spain's long war against Napoleon begins.

events.title: Dalton's Atoms
events.body: John Dalton argues that each element is made of its own kind of atom, with its own weight — the start of modern chemistry.

events.title: Beethoven's Fifth
events.body: In a freezing four-hour concert in Vienna, Beethoven premieres his Fifth and Sixth symphonies. The Fifth's four-note opening becomes the most famous in music.

events.title: The May Revolution
events.body: Buenos Aires removes the Spanish viceroy and sets up its own government — the start of Argentina's independence.

events.title: Food in a Tin
events.body: Nicolas Appert publishes his method of preserving food in sealed, boiled containers, for which France paid him a prize. The same year a British patent covers tin cans.

events.title: The Dandy
events.body: Beau Brummell makes plain dark coats, long trousers and a perfectly tied cravat the height of men's style in Regency London — a forerunner of the modern suit.

events.title: Kamehameha Unites Hawaii
events.body: The last independent island, Kauaʻi, accepts Kamehameha's rule, and the Hawaiian Islands become one kingdom.

events.title: The Cry of Dolores
events.body: Father Miguel Hidalgo rings his church bell and calls his parishioners to rise against Spanish rule — the start of Mexico's war of independence.

events.title: The Massacre of the Mamluks
events.body: Muhammad Ali invites the leaders of the Mamluks, Egypt's old military caste, to a ceremony at the Cairo Citadel and has them killed.

events.title: Napoleon Invades Russia
events.body: The Grande Armée of more than half a million men crosses into Russia. Moscow burns, winter comes, and only a small fraction return.

events.title: The Fourth Frontier War
events.body: British and colonial forces drive about 20,000 Xhosa people across the Fish River from the Zuurveld, and found a military post at Grahamstown, now Makhanda.

events.title: Grimms' Fairy Tales
events.body: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm publish the first volume of the folk tales they collected, including Hansel and Gretel and Snow White.

events.title: Pride and Prejudice
events.body: Jane Austen's novel of Elizabeth Bennet and Mr Darcy is published anonymously, 'by the author of Sense and Sensibility'.

events.title: Crossing the Blue Mountains
events.body: Three settlers find a way over the Blue Mountains west of Sydney, opening the inland to sheep and cattle — and to the dispossession of its Aboriginal peoples.

events.title: Rebels in the Forbidden City
events.body: Members of the Eight Trigrams sect break into the imperial palace in Beijing before they are beaten back — a sign of the Qing dynasty's weakening grip.

events.title: Kean's Shylock
events.body: Unknown actor Edmund Kean plays Shylock at Drury Lane as a man wronged rather than a comic villain, and becomes a star overnight.

events.title: The Third of May 1808
events.body: Goya paints the French firing squad and its victims, one with arms flung wide. It has been called the first modern painting of war.

events.title: The Star-Spangled Banner
events.body: After watching the British bombard Fort McHenry through the night, Francis Scott Key writes the poem that becomes the US national anthem.

events.title: The Kandyan Convention
events.body: The chiefs of the Kingdom of Kandy hand it to Britain, bringing the whole of Sri Lanka under British rule.

events.title: Tambora Erupts
events.body: The largest volcanic eruption in recorded history blows apart Mount Tambora in Indonesia, killing tens of thousands. Its ash cools the whole planet.

events.title: The Congress of Vienna
events.body: Europe's powers sign the treaty that redraws the map after Napoleon and keeps a rough peace among them for decades.

events.title: Waterloo
events.body: Wellington's army and the Prussians defeat Napoleon in Belgium, ending his hundred days back in power. He is exiled to St Helena.

events.title: The Map That Changed the World
events.body: William Smith publishes the first geological map of a whole country, tracing England's and Wales's rock layers by the fossils in them.

events.title: Sarah Baartman Dies in Paris
events.body: Sarah Baartman, a Khoikhoi woman taken from the Cape and displayed to paying crowds in London and Paris as a curiosity, dies aged about 26. Her remains are shown in a Paris museum for over 150 years, until they are returned to South Africa in 2002.

events.title: Bussa's Rebellion
events.body: Enslaved people in Barbados rise in the island's largest revolt, led by the African-born Bussa. It is crushed within days.

events.title: The Year Without a Summer
events.body: With Tambora's ash in the sky, snow falls in June in New England and crops fail across Europe and North America. Famine and disease follow.

events.title: The Stethoscope
events.body: Too embarrassed to press his ear to a young woman's chest, René Laennec rolls paper into a tube — and hears her heart more clearly than ever.

events.title: Shaka Becomes King
events.body: Shaka takes power over the Zulu and, through war and alliance, builds them into the strongest kingdom in south-eastern Africa.

events.title: San Martín Crosses the Andes
events.body: José de San Martín leads an army over mountain passes nearly 4,000 metres high and defeats the Spanish at Chacabuco. Chile declares independence a year later.

events.title: The Running Machine
events.body: Karl Drais rides his two-wheeled, pedal-less 'running machine' out of Mannheim — the ancestor of the bicycle. Some link it to horses lost in the Year Without a Summer.

events.title: Frankenstein
events.body: Mary Shelley's novel, begun during a ghost-story contest on a cold, wet summer by Lake Geneva in 1816, is published anonymously.

events.title: The Fall of Diriyah
events.body: An Egyptian army sent by Muhammad Ali destroys the Saudi capital, Diriyah, ending the first Saudi state.

events.title: Raffles Founds Singapore
events.body: Stamford Raffles signs a treaty with the ruler of Johor to set up a British trading post on the island of Singapore.

events.title: The Battle of Grahamstown
events.body: The Xhosa prophet Makhanda leads thousands of warriors against the British garrison at Grahamstown. They are beaten back; Makhanda later surrenders and drowns escaping Robben Island.

events.title: Bolívar Wins at Boyacá
events.body: Simón Bolívar's army defeats the Spanish in the Andes, freeing New Granada. Bolívar becomes president of Gran Colombia.

events.title: Peterloo
events.body: Cavalry charge a peaceful crowd of about 60,000 demanding the vote in Manchester. Between 15 and 18 people are killed and hundreds injured.

events.title: Antarctica Sighted
events.body: Fabian von Bellingshausen's Russian expedition sees an ice shelf of the Antarctic mainland. British and American sailors report land within days or months.

events.title: The 1820 Settlers
events.body: About 4,000 British settlers land at Algoa Bay, placed on the frontier as a buffer against the Xhosa.

events.title: The Greek War of Independence
events.body: Greeks rise against Ottoman rule. Volunteers from across Europe, including Lord Byron, join the cause; Greece wins independence in 1830.

events.title: Napoleon Dies on St Helena
events.body: Napoleon dies in exile on a remote island in the South Atlantic, aged 51.

events.title: Mexico Becomes Independent
events.body: After eleven years of war, Agustín de Iturbide's army enters Mexico City and Spanish rule ends. Iturbide soon makes himself emperor.

events.title: Liberia Founded
events.body: Freed Black Americans sent by the American Colonization Society settle at Cape Mesurado in West Africa. Liberia declares independence in 1847.

events.title: Brazil Becomes Independent
events.body: Prince Pedro, son of the Portuguese king, declares Brazil independent by the Ipiranga stream: 'Independence or death!' He becomes its emperor.

events.title: Hieroglyphs Deciphered
events.body: Using the Rosetta Stone's parallel texts, Jean-François Champollion shows how Egyptian hieroglyphs work. A script used for more than three thousand years can be read again.

events.title: The United Provinces of Central America
events.body: Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua and Costa Rica declare themselves independent of Mexico as one federation. It breaks apart by 1841.

events.title: The Monroe Doctrine
events.body: President Monroe warns European powers against new colonies in the Americas — a claim to a US sphere of influence that lasts.

events.title: The Asante Defeat the British
events.body: At Nsamankow, an Asante army defeats a British force; the governor, Sir Charles MacCarthy, is killed.

events.title: The First Anglo-Burmese War
events.body: Britain declares war on Burma. By the 1826 peace, Burma has lost Assam, Arakan and Tenasserim.

events.title: Ode to Joy
events.body: Beethoven, by now almost totally deaf, premieres his Ninth Symphony in Vienna. A singer turns him round to see the applause he cannot hear.

events.title: Ayacucho
events.body: Antonio José de Sucre's army defeats the last major Spanish force in South America, high in the Peruvian Andes.

events.title: The Java War
events.body: Prince Diponegoro leads a rebellion against Dutch rule in Java. In five years of war, some 200,000 Javanese die.

events.title: The First Public Railway
events.body: George Stephenson drives Locomotion No. 1 on the opening day of the Stockton and Darlington Railway, the first public railway to use steam locomotives.

events.title: The Erie Canal
events.body: A canal of more than 500 kilometres links the Great Lakes to the Hudson River and the sea, and makes New York America's greatest port.

events.title: The Decembrists
events.body: Army officers in St Petersburg refuse to swear loyalty to the new tsar, Nicholas I, and demand a constitution. The revolt is crushed with cannon fire.

events.title: The Janissaries Abolished
events.body: Sultan Mahmud II's new army destroys the rebelling Janissaries, the Ottoman Empire's old elite infantry, clearing the way for reform.

events.title: The First Photograph
events.body: In 1826 or 1827, Nicéphore Niépce fixes the view from his upstairs window on a pewter plate coated with bitumen, in an exposure of hours or days. It is the oldest surviving camera photograph.

events.title: Ordinance 50
events.body: The Cape government frees Khoikhoi and other free people of colour from pass laws and forced labour contracts, giving them equality before the law.

events.title: The Brahmo Samaj
events.body: Ram Mohan Roy founds a Hindu reform movement in Calcutta that rejects idol worship and caste, and campaigns for women's rights.

events.title: Shaka Assassinated
events.body: Shaka is stabbed to death by his half-brothers at KwaDukuza. One of them, Dingane, becomes king.

events.title: The Black War
events.body: The governor of Van Diemen's Land declares martial law against Aboriginal Tasmanians. By the mid-1830s the few hundred survivors have been moved to Flinders Island.

events.title: Braille
events.body: Louis Braille, blind since childhood, publishes his system of raised dots that lets blind people read and write by touch.

events.title: Sati Banned
events.body: The British authorities in Bengal outlaw sati, the burning of widows on their husbands' funeral pyres, after years of campaigning by Ram Mohan Roy and others.

events.title: Greece Becomes Independent
events.body: Britain, France and Russia agree in London that Greece will be an independent kingdom.

events.title: The Battle of Hernani
events.body: Victor Hugo's verse drama breaks the old rules of French tragedy. Night after night, young Romantics and traditionalists fight in the theatre.

events.title: The Book of Mormon
events.body: Joseph Smith publishes the Book of Mormon in upstate New York. Days later he founds the church that becomes the Latter Day Saint movement.

events.title: The Indian Removal Act
events.body: The US Congress authorises forcing Native nations out of the south-east. On the Cherokee 'Trail of Tears' of 1838–39, thousands die on the march west.

events.title: The Cultivation System
events.body: The Dutch force Javanese villages to grow coffee, sugar and indigo for the colonial government. The profits fill the Dutch treasury; famines follow in Java.

events.title: France Invades Algeria
events.body: French troops take Algiers. Colonial rule lasts 132 years; Emir Abdelkader leads resistance until 1847.

events.title: The July Revolution
events.body: Three days of street fighting in Paris drive out King Charles X, who had tried to silence the press and dissolve parliament.

events.title: The First Intercity Railway
events.body: The Liverpool and Manchester Railway opens, running entirely on steam. On the first day, the politician William Huskisson is hit by Stephenson's Rocket and dies.

events.title: Liberty Leading the People
events.body: Delacroix paints a bare-breasted Liberty carrying the tricolour over the barricades of the July Revolution.

events.title: The November Uprising
events.body: Young Polish officers rise against Russian rule in Warsaw. The revolt is crushed in 1831 and thousands go into exile. Chopin, who left Warsaw weeks before, never returns home.

events.title: The Great Wave
events.body: Around 1831, Hokusai publishes a woodblock print of a huge wave about to crash over boats, with Mount Fuji tiny in the distance.

events.title: Nat Turner's Rebellion
events.body: Enslaved preacher Nat Turner leads a revolt in Virginia; about 60 white people are killed. In reprisal, many more Black people are killed, and Southern states pass harsher slave laws.

events.title: Electromagnetic Induction
events.body: Michael Faraday shows that a changing magnetic field makes an electric current flow — the principle behind every generator and transformer.

events.title: The Baptist War
events.body: Baptist deacon Samuel Sharpe leads a strike that becomes an uprising of up to 60,000 enslaved people in Jamaica. Hundreds are killed or executed, Sharpe among them; Britain abolishes slavery two years later.

events.title: The Voyage of the Beagle
events.body: Twenty-two-year-old Charles Darwin sails from Plymouth on a five-year survey voyage round the world, including the Galápagos and the Cape.

events.title: Slavery Abolished in the British Empire
events.body: Britain's Slavery Abolition Act frees enslaved people across the empire from 1834 — though most must first serve years of 'apprenticeship'. Slave owners, not the enslaved, are paid compensation.

events.title: The Sixth Frontier War
events.body: Xhosa forces cross into the Cape Colony after years of land seizures. In 1835, King Hintsa is shot dead while held by British forces.

events.title: Macaulay's Minute
events.body: Thomas Macaulay argues that Indians should be educated in English. The government adopts the policy, shaping India's elite — and its languages — for generations.

events.title: Zwangendaba Crosses the Zambezi
events.body: Fleeing the wars of the Mfecane, the Ngoni leader Zwangendaba leads his people north across the Zambezi — by tradition during a solar eclipse. Ngoni kingdoms grow up in today's Malawi, Zambia and Tanzania.

events.title: Darwin in the Galápagos
events.body: The Beagle reaches the Galápagos. Darwin spends five weeks among the islands' finches, mockingbirds and giant tortoises, which later help shape his theory.

events.title: The Great Trek
events.body: Thousands of Dutch-speaking settlers leave the Cape Colony with their wagons, livestock and servants, moving into the interior beyond British rule.

events.title: Portugal Bans the Slave Trade
events.body: Portugal outlaws the export of enslaved people from its colonies. The illegal trade from Angola continues for decades.

events.title: Victoria Becomes Queen
events.body: Eighteen-year-old Victoria succeeds her uncle. She reigns for 63 years over a growing empire.

events.title: Myall Creek
events.body: Stockmen murder about 28 Wirrayaraay people at Myall Creek in New South Wales. Seven of them are hanged — the first time colonists are executed for killing Aboriginal people.

events.title: Emancipation at the Cape
events.body: Apprenticeship ends and some 39,000 formerly enslaved people at the Cape are fully free. 1 December is still remembered in Cape Town.

events.title: Blood River
events.body: At the Ncome River, about 470 Voortrekkers in a laager defeat a Zulu army of thousands with guns and cannon; around 3,000 Zulu are killed. Afrikaner nationalism later makes the day sacred; today 16 December is the Day of Reconciliation.

events.title: The Daguerreotype
events.body: The French government announces Louis Daguerre's photographic process and gives it 'free to the world'. Within months, portrait studios open across Europe and America.

events.title: The First Opium War
events.body: After China's commissioner Lin Zexu destroys British opium, Britain goes to war to keep the trade open. China is forced to give up Hong Kong in the Treaty of Nanking in 1842.

events.title: The Tanzimat
events.body: The Ottoman edict of Gülhane promises security of life and property, fair taxes and equality for non-Muslims — the start of the Tanzimat reforms.

events.title: The Treaty of Waitangi
events.body: British officials and Māori chiefs sign a treaty founding New Zealand as a colony. The English and Māori versions say different things about sovereignty, and the dispute continues.

events.title: The Penny Black
events.body: Britain issues the world's first adhesive postage stamp. For one penny, a letter can go anywhere in the country.

events.title: The Sultan Moves to Zanzibar
events.body: Sultan Said of Oman moves his court to Zanzibar. Clove plantations worked by enslaved people spread, and the East African slave trade grows to its height.

events.title: The Guano Age
events.body: Peru begins exporting seabird droppings from its offshore islands as fertiliser. The boom makes fortunes; Chinese indentured labourers dig it out in brutal conditions.

events.title: The White Rajah of Sarawak
events.body: Englishman James Brooke is made Rajah of Sarawak on Borneo. His family rules it for a century.

events.title: The Retreat from Kabul
events.body: A British army and thousands of camp followers retreating from Kabul in winter are destroyed in the mountain passes. Almost no one reaches Jalalabad.

events.title: Nabucco
events.body: Verdi's opera premieres at La Scala. Its chorus of Hebrew slaves longing for home, 'Va, pensiero', becomes linked with Italians' wish for a nation of their own.

events.title: Executions in Bukhara
events.body: The Emir of Bukhara beheads two British officers, Stoddart and Conolly — casualties of the 'Great Game' between Britain and Russia for Central Asia.

events.title: Hong Kong Ceded
events.body: The Treaty of Nanking ends the First Opium War. China pays an indemnity, opens five ports and hands Hong Kong Island to Britain — the first of what Chinese historians call the unequal treaties.

events.title: The First Computer Program
events.body: Ada Lovelace publishes notes on Charles Babbage's planned Analytical Engine, including a method for it to calculate Bernoulli numbers — often called the first computer program.

events.title: Britain Annexes Natal
events.body: Britain takes over the Voortrekker republic of Natalia. Many trekkers move on again, over the Drakensberg.

events.title: A Christmas Carol
events.body: Charles Dickens publishes his ghost story of the miser Scrooge. It sells out by Christmas Eve and helps shape how Christmas is kept.

events.title: The Dominican Republic Is Born
events.body: The eastern part of Hispaniola declares independence from Haiti.

events.title: The Báb
events.body: In Shiraz, a young merchant declares himself the Báb, 'the Gate', heralding a new messenger of God. His movement leads to the Baháʼí Faith.

events.title: What Hath God Wrought
events.body: Samuel Morse sends a Bible verse by electric telegraph from Washington to Baltimore. News that once took days now takes moments.

events.title: The First International Match
events.body: The United States and Canada play cricket in New York — thought to be the first international match in any modern team sport.

events.title: Indians Arrive in Trinidad
events.body: The ship Fatel Razack lands the first indentured labourers from India in Trinidad. About 140,000 follow; Indian Arrival Day is a public holiday.

events.title: The Great Famine in Ireland
events.body: Potato blight destroys Ireland's main food crop for years in a row. About a million people die and another million emigrate, while food is still exported from the island.

events.title: Neptune Found by Mathematics
events.body: Johann Galle in Berlin finds Neptune within a degree of where Urbain Le Verrier calculated it must be, from wobbles in Uranus's orbit.

events.title: Ether Day
events.body: At Massachusetts General Hospital, a dentist puts a patient to sleep with ether while a surgeon removes a tumour from his neck. Surgery without pain begins.

events.title: Wash Your Hands
events.body: Ignaz Semmelweis orders doctors in his Vienna maternity ward to wash their hands in chlorine solution. Deaths from childbed fever fall sharply, but colleagues reject his idea.

events.title: Liberia Declares Independence
events.body: Liberia becomes Africa's first modern republic. Power stays with the settlers from America rather than the peoples already living there.

events.title: The Caste War of Yucatán
events.body: Maya communities rise against the white and mestizo elite of Yucatán. Fighting continues, on and off, for over fifty years.

events.title: Jane Eyre
events.body: Charlotte Brontë, writing as 'Currer Bell', publishes her novel of a poor governess who insists on her own worth.

events.title: The California Gold Rush
events.body: Gold is found at Sutter's Mill. Some 300,000 people pour into California; its Native peoples are driven off and killed in large numbers.

events.title: Mexico Loses Half Its Land
events.body: The Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo ends the Mexican–American War. Mexico gives up about half its territory, including California and the south-west.

events.title: The Communist Manifesto
events.body: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels publish a short pamphlet in London: 'Workers of the world, unite!'

sources.title: Manifesto of the Communist Party, chapter 1

events.title: The Revolutions of 1848
events.body: A revolution in Paris topples King Louis-Philippe and sets off risings across Europe, from Berlin and Vienna to Budapest and Milan. Most are crushed within a year.

events.title: The Hungarian Revolution
events.body: In Pest, the poet Sándor Petőfi reads his National Song to the crowds and Hungary rises for self-rule. The revolution is crushed in 1849 with the help of a Russian army.

events.title: Snow on the Equator
events.body: Missionary Johannes Rebmann is the first European to see Kilimanjaro. Geographers in London mock his report of snow so near the equator.

events.title: Seneca Falls
events.body: Some 300 people meet in New York State for the first women's rights convention. Its declaration demands, among much else, women's right to vote. Frederick Douglass speaks in support.

events.title: Harriet Tubman Escapes
events.body: Harriet Tubman flees slavery in Maryland. She goes back again and again, guiding dozens of others to freedom on the Underground Railroad.

events.title: The Taiping Rebellion
events.body: Hong Xiuquan, who believes he is the younger brother of Jesus, launches a rebellion against the Qing dynasty. In the civil war that follows, an estimated 20 to 30 million people die.

events.title: The Crystal Palace
events.body: The Great Exhibition opens in London in a vast building of iron and glass. Six million visitors come to see the industry of the world.

events.title: Moby-Dick
events.body: Herman Melville's novel of Captain Ahab's hunt for the white whale is published in London, then New York. It sells poorly; its fame comes long after.

events.title: The Boer Republics
events.body: Britain recognises the independence of the Transvaal at the Sand River; the Orange Free State follows in 1854.

events.title: Uncle Tom's Cabin
events.body: Harriet Beecher Stowe's anti-slavery novel sells hundreds of thousands of copies in its first year and hardens feeling against slavery in the North.

events.title: Umar Tall's Jihad
events.body: El Hadj Umar Tall launches a holy war and builds an empire across today's Senegal, Guinea and Mali, until he collides with the French.

events.title: India's First Train
events.body: A train runs from Bombay to Thane. Within fifty years India has one of the largest railway networks in the world.

events.title: The Cape Franchise
events.body: The Cape Colony gets an elected parliament. The vote depends on property or wages, not race, though the bar keeps most Black people out.

events.title: The Black Ships
events.body: US Commodore Perry sails warships into Edo Bay and demands that Japan open its ports. Japan's two centuries of near-isolation end.

events.title: The Broad Street Pump
events.body: When cholera kills hundreds in Soho, John Snow maps the deaths, traces them to one water pump and has its handle removed — a founding moment of epidemiology.

events.title: The Charge of the Light Brigade
events.body: In the Crimean War, a misunderstood order sends British light cavalry straight into Russian guns at Balaclava.

events.title: The Lady with the Lamp
events.body: Florence Nightingale and her nurses arrive at the army hospital at Scutari. Her later statistics on needless deaths change hospitals and nursing.

events.title: Peru Frees Its Slaves
events.body: President Ramón Castilla abolishes slavery in Peru, paying owners compensation from guano money.

events.title: The Eureka Stockade
events.body: Gold miners at Ballarat, angry at licence fees and police, build a stockade under the Southern Cross flag. Troops storm it and more than twenty die; many Australians see it as a birth of their democracy.

events.title: Tennyson's Light Brigade
events.body: Tennyson's poem 'Into the valley of Death / Rode the six hundred' is published weeks after the charge.

events.title: Tewodros II Crowned
events.body: Kassa Hailu, a soldier from the border country, is crowned Emperor Tewodros II and sets out to reunite Ethiopia after decades of rival lords.

events.title: The Bowring Treaty
events.body: King Mongkut of Siam opens his country to British trade on British terms — part of how Siam keeps its independence while its neighbours are colonised.

events.title: Mosi-oa-Tunya
events.body: David Livingstone is taken to the great falls on the Zambezi that the Kololo call Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the smoke that thunders'. He names them after Queen Victoria.

events.title: The Xhosa Cattle-Killing
events.body: The young prophet Nongqawuse says that if the Xhosa kill their cattle and destroy their crops, the dead will rise and the British will be swept away. Tens of thousands starve in 1857.

events.title: Cheap Steel
events.body: Henry Bessemer patents a way to blow air through molten iron to make steel quickly and cheaply — the metal of railways, ships and skyscrapers.

events.title: The Cage Crinoline
events.body: A light frame of steel hoops replaces layers of petticoats, and skirts swell to enormous widths across Europe and America.

events.title: William Walker Rules Nicaragua
events.body: An American adventurer with a private army makes himself president of Nicaragua and brings back slavery. Central American armies drive him out within a year.

events.title: Madame Bovary
events.body: Gustave Flaubert's novel of a doctor's wife who seeks escape in affairs is published as a book, after he is tried and acquitted for offending public morals.

events.title: The Indian Rebellion
events.body: Indian soldiers of the East India Company mutiny at Meerut, and revolt spreads across northern India. After it is crushed, the British Crown takes direct rule.

events.title: The House of Worth
events.body: Charles Frederick Worth opens his fashion house in Paris, showing designs on live models and sewing his name into the clothes — the birth of haute couture.

events.title: The First Free State–Basotho War
events.body: Moshoeshoe's Basotho hold off the Orange Free State's forces in the first of a series of wars over land along the Caledon River.

events.title: The Great Stink
events.body: In a hot summer, the sewage-filled Thames smells so bad that Parliament acts. Joseph Bazalgette's new sewers follow, and help end London's cholera epidemics.

events.title: The First Oil Well
events.body: Edwin Drake strikes oil at 21 metres in Titusville, Pennsylvania. The oil age begins.

events.title: The Carrington Event
events.body: Richard Carrington sees a white flare on the Sun. Next day, auroras are seen near the tropics and telegraph lines spark and fail — the largest solar storm on record.

events.title: On the Origin of Species
events.body: Charles Darwin publishes his theory of evolution by natural selection. Booksellers snap up the whole first printing before publication day.

events.title: The Expedition of the Thousand
events.body: Garibaldi lands in Sicily with about a thousand red-shirted volunteers and conquers the south of Italy for the cause of unification.

events.title: The Checkered Game of Life
events.body: Lithographer Milton Bradley launches a board game in which players move through virtue and vice towards 'Happy Old Age'. It sells tens of thousands in its first year.

events.title: Max Havelaar
events.body: A former colonial official writing as Multatuli publishes a novel exposing the abuses of Dutch rule in Java.

events.title: The Damascus Massacre
events.body: After civil war in Mount Lebanon, mobs kill thousands of Christians in Damascus. The exiled Algerian leader Abdelkader shelters many in his home.

events.title: The Indian Penal Code
events.body: Britain enacts a criminal code drafted under Macaulay. India used it until 2024; Pakistan and Bangladesh still do.

events.title: The Summer Palace Burned
events.body: At the end of the Second Opium War, British and French troops loot and burn the Old Summer Palace in Beijing, with its gardens and treasures.

events.title: Indentured Indians Arrive in Natal
events.body: The ship Truro lands the first indentured labourers from India at Durban, to work on the sugar plantations. Over the next fifty years about 150,000 follow.

events.title: The Serfs Freed
events.body: Tsar Alexander II frees Russia's serfs — about 23 million people bound to the land — though they must pay for the plots they receive.

events.title: Italy Unified
events.body: The Kingdom of Italy is proclaimed in Turin. Rome joins in 1870.

events.title: The American Civil War Begins
events.body: Confederate guns fire on Fort Sumter in Charleston harbour. Four years of war over slavery and union follow; between about 620,000 and 750,000 soldiers die.

events.title: Britain Annexes Lagos
events.body: Britain takes Lagos, citing the slave trade. It becomes the foothold for colonial Nigeria.

events.title: Cinco de Mayo
events.body: At Puebla, a Mexican army beats back French invaders sent by Napoleon III. France takes Mexico City the next year.

events.title: France Takes Cochinchina
events.body: In the Treaty of Saigon, Vietnam's emperor gives up three southern provinces to France — the start of French Indochina.

events.title: Les Misérables
events.body: Victor Hugo, in exile on Guernsey, publishes his vast novel of the former convict Jean Valjean and the poor of Paris.

events.title: The Source of the Nile
events.body: John Hanning Speke reaches the falls where the Nile flows out of Lake Victoria, settling a question geographers had argued over since ancient times.

events.title: The Emancipation Proclamation
events.body: Lincoln declares enslaved people in the rebel states free, and opens the Union army to Black soldiers.

events.title: The Underground
events.body: The world's first underground railway opens in London, with steam trains running through shallow tunnels between Paddington and Farringdon.

events.title: The Salon des Refusés
events.body: Paintings rejected by the official Salon are shown in a separate exhibition. Crowds jeer Manet's Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe — and modern art has its first scandal.

events.title: The Invasion of the Waikato
events.body: British troops cross into the Waikato, heart of the Māori King Movement. Huge areas of Māori land are confiscated after the war.

events.title: Blackbirding
events.body: The first ship brings Pacific Islanders to Queensland's sugar plantations. Over the next forty years about 60,000 follow, many tricked or kidnapped from today's Vanuatu and Solomon Islands.

events.title: Lincoln Proclaims Thanksgiving
events.body: In the middle of the Civil War, and after seventeen years of letters from the editor Sarah Josepha Hale, Lincoln sets the last Thursday of November as a national day of thanksgiving.

events.title: The Football Association
events.body: Clubs meet at a London tavern to agree one set of rules for football. Handling and hacking are soon ruled out, and rugby goes its own way.

events.title: The Gettysburg Address
events.body: At a battlefield cemetery, Lincoln speaks for about two minutes of 'a new birth of freedom' and government 'of the people, by the people, for the people'.

events.title: The First Geneva Convention
events.body: Twelve states agree to protect wounded soldiers and the medics who treat them, under the sign of a red cross. Henry Dunant had seen the wounded left to die at Solferino.

events.title: The Paraguayan War
events.body: Paraguay goes to war with Brazil, and soon Argentina and Uruguay as well. By 1870 it has lost a large part of its population; estimates vary widely.

events.title: Mendel's Peas
events.body: Gregor Mendel, a friar in Brno, presents years of pea-breeding experiments showing how traits are inherited. He is ignored until 1900.

events.title: Lincoln Assassinated
events.body: Five days after the Confederate surrender, Lincoln is shot at Ford's Theatre in Washington by the actor John Wilkes Booth.

events.title: The First Memorial Day
events.body: In Charleston, freed people rebury Union soldiers who died in a prison camp at the city's racecourse, and thousands march to honour them — often called the first Memorial Day.

events.title: Russia Takes Tashkent
events.body: General Chernyayev's troops storm Tashkent. It becomes the capital of Russian Turkestan as the tsar's empire takes Central Asia.

events.title: Juneteenth
events.body: Union General Gordon Granger announces in Galveston, Texas, that all enslaved people are free — two and a half years after the Emancipation Proclamation.

events.title: Maxwell's Equations
events.body: James Clerk Maxwell shows that electricity, magnetism and light are one thing — waves in an electromagnetic field — and predicts invisible waves that become radio.

events.title: The Morant Bay Rebellion
events.body: Paul Bogle leads a protest over poverty and injustice in Jamaica. Governor Eyre's martial law kills hundreds; Bogle is hanged, and Jamaica loses its elected assembly.

events.title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
events.body: Oxford mathematician Charles Dodgson, as Lewis Carroll, publishes the story he first told to a girl called Alice Liddell on a boating trip.

events.title: The Thirteenth Amendment
events.body: Slavery is abolished throughout the United States. Within months, Southern states pass 'Black Codes' to control the freed people.

sources.title: 13th Amendment to the US Constitution: Abolition of Slavery

events.title: Maximilian Executed
events.body: Maximilian, the Austrian archduke France had made Emperor of Mexico, is shot by Benito Juárez's republicans at Querétaro.

events.title: Antiseptic Surgery
events.body: Joseph Lister, building on Pasteur's germ theory, publishes his results with carbolic acid in Glasgow: far fewer wounds turn septic.

events.title: The Eureka Diamond
events.body: A farm boy near Hopetown finds a shiny stone; it is a 21-carat diamond. Within a few years, the diamond fields transform southern Africa.

events.title: Canada Confederation
events.body: Three British colonies unite as the Dominion of Canada.

events.title: Dynamite
events.body: Alfred Nobel patents dynamite, making nitroglycerine safe to handle. It builds railways and tunnels — and fortunes; he leaves his to found the Nobel Prizes.

events.title: Das Kapital
events.body: Karl Marx publishes the first volume of Capital, his analysis of how capitalism makes profit from labour.

events.title: The Meiji Restoration
events.body: Rule by the shogun ends and power returns to the young Emperor Meiji. Japan sets out to modernise at speed.

sources.title: The Charter Oath (1868)
sources.publisher: "The World and Japan" Database, University of Tokyo

events.title: Basutoland Under British Protection
events.body: Losing land to the Orange Free State, Moshoeshoe asks Britain for protection. Basutoland, later Lesotho, survives as a separate country.

events.title: Maqdala
events.body: A British expedition storms Tewodros's mountain fortress; the emperor shoots himself rather than be captured. Soldiers loot manuscripts and treasures, many still in British collections.

events.title: Decoration Day
events.body: At General John Logan's call, Americans decorate the graves of the Union dead with flowers. The main ceremony is at Arlington.

events.title: The Execution of Emperor Maximilian
events.body: Manet paints the firing squad several times over, dressing the soldiers like French troops. The French government bans the work from being shown.

events.title: Cuba's Ten Years' War
events.body: Planter Carlos Manuel de Céspedes frees his slaves and declares Cuba's independence. Ten years of war against Spain follow.

events.title: The Periodic Table
events.body: Dmitri Mendeleev arranges the elements by weight and properties — and leaves gaps for elements not yet found, predicting what they will be like.

events.title: The Transcontinental Railroad
events.body: A golden spike joins the railway lines from east and west at Promontory Summit, Utah. Thousands of Chinese labourers built much of the western section.

events.title: Margarine
events.body: French chemist Hippolyte Mège-Mouriès invents a cheap substitute for butter, answering a prize offered by Napoleon III.

events.title: War and Peace
events.body: Leo Tolstoy completes his novel of Russian families living through Napoleon's invasion.

events.title: The Suez Canal Opens
events.body: A canal across the isthmus of Suez joins the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, cutting the sea route from Europe to Asia by thousands of kilometres. Egyptian forced labourers dug much of it.

events.title: America's First Federal Holidays
events.body: Congress makes New Year's Day, Independence Day, Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays for federal workers in Washington — the first federal holidays.

events.title: Papal Infallibility
events.body: The First Vatican Council declares that the Pope cannot err when he defines doctrine. Two months later Italian troops take Rome.

events.title: The German Empire
events.body: After crushing France, Prussia's king is proclaimed German Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles. Bismarck's united Germany is born.

events.title: The Paris Commune
events.body: Working-class Paris rises and governs itself for two months. In the 'Bloody Week' that ends it, French troops kill thousands of Communards.

events.title: The Bank Holidays Act
events.body: Banker and MP John Lubbock's act makes Easter Monday, Whit Monday, the first Monday in August and Boxing Day bank holidays in England, Wales and Ireland, with a separate list for Scotland. Grateful workers call them 'St Lubbock's Days'.

events.title: The Kimberley Diamond Rush
events.body: Diamonds are found on Colesberg Kopje. Thousands dig by hand what becomes the Big Hole, and Cecil Rhodes begins building the fortune behind De Beers.

events.title: The Great Chicago Fire
events.body: Fire burns for two days through a city built of wood, killing about 300 people and leaving some 100,000 homeless.

events.title: Dr Livingstone, I Presume?
events.body: Journalist Henry Morton Stanley, sent by a New York newspaper, finds the missing David Livingstone at Ujiji on Lake Tanganyika.

events.title: The First National Park
events.body: The US Congress makes Yellowstone, with its geysers and hot springs, the world's first national park.

events.title: The First Football International
events.body: Scotland and England draw 0–0 at a cricket ground in Glasgow, in front of about 4,000 spectators.

events.title: The Aceh War
events.body: The Dutch declare war on the Sultanate of Aceh in northern Sumatra. Resistance continues for decades.

events.title: Blue Jeans
events.body: Levi Strauss and tailor Jacob Davis patent work trousers strengthened with copper rivets — the first blue jeans.

events.title: The Zanzibar Slave Market Closes
events.body: Under British pressure, Sultan Barghash signs a treaty ending the sea trade in enslaved people. An Anglican cathedral is built on the site of the old market.

events.title: Kumasi Burned
events.body: In the Third Anglo-Ashanti War, British troops occupy and burn the Asante capital.

events.title: Impressionism
events.body: Monet, Renoir, Degas, Cézanne and others hold their own exhibition in Paris. A critic mocks Monet's Impression, Sunrise — and the name 'Impressionists' sticks.

events.title: Fiji Ceded to Britain
events.body: King Cakobau and other chiefs cede Fiji to Britain.

events.title: The Palais Garnier
events.body: Paris's gilded new opera house opens after fourteen years of building, with a lake beneath it that later inspires The Phantom of the Opera.

events.title: Afrikaans in Print
events.body: In Paarl, the Genootskap van Regte Afrikaners is founded to have Afrikaans recognised as a language. Its newspaper, Die Afrikaanse Patriot, follows.

events.title: Tonga's Constitution
events.body: King George Tupou I grants Tonga a constitution. Tonga is never colonised, though it becomes a British protectorate from 1900 to 1970.

events.title: Britain Buys Into Suez
events.body: With Egypt deep in debt, Prime Minister Disraeli buys the Khedive's shares in the Suez Canal Company for £4 million.

events.title: Korea Forced Open
events.body: Japan, using the gunboat tactics once used on it, forces Korea to sign the unequal Treaty of Ganghwa.

events.title: The Telephone
events.body: Three days after his patent is granted, Alexander Graham Bell speaks to his assistant down a wire: 'Mr. Watson, come here — I want to see you.'

events.title: The Little Bighorn
events.body: Lakota, Northern Cheyenne and Arapaho warriors led by Sitting Bull and Crazy Horse wipe out Custer's command of the US 7th Cavalry.

events.title: The Great Famine of 1876–78
events.body: Drought and failed monsoons bring famine to southern India while grain is still exported; millions die. Northern China suffers a famine on the same scale.

events.title: The Ring at Bayreuth
events.body: Wagner opens his own festival theatre with the first complete performance of The Ring of the Nibelung, four operas over about fifteen hours.

events.title: Porfirio Díaz Takes Power
events.body: General Porfirio Díaz seizes power in Mexico and, with one short break, rules until 1911. Railways and foreign money pour in while land is concentrated in few hands.

events.title: The First Ottoman Constitution
events.body: The Ottoman Empire adopts a constitution and parliament. Sultan Abdul Hamid II suspends both in 1878.

events.title: Empress of India
events.body: At a vast durbar in Delhi, Queen Victoria is proclaimed Empress of India — while famine is killing millions in the south.

events.title: Swan Lake
events.body: Tchaikovsky's first ballet premieres at the Bolshoi in Moscow to a cool reception. Its 1895 revival makes it one of the most performed ballets in the world.

events.title: The First Test Match
events.body: Australia beat England by 45 runs at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in what is now counted as the first Test.

events.title: Britain Annexes the Transvaal
events.body: A British official rides into Pretoria and annexes the bankrupt South African Republic. The Boers bide their time.

events.title: The First Wimbledon
events.body: The All England Croquet Club holds a lawn tennis championship to pay for a pony roller. Spencer Gore wins in front of about 200 people.

events.title: The Moons of Mars
events.body: Asaph Hall at the US Naval Observatory discovers Mars's two small moons, which he names Phobos and Deimos, Fear and Dread.

events.title: Stanley Crosses Africa
events.body: After 999 days and the deaths of more than half his party, Henry Morton Stanley follows the Congo River to the Atlantic at Boma.

events.title: The Satsuma Rebellion
events.body: Samurai led by Saigō Takamori revolt against the Meiji government's reforms. The new conscript army defeats them, and Saigō dies at Shiroyama.

events.title: The Phonograph
events.body: Thomas Edison records himself reciting 'Mary had a little lamb' on tinfoil and plays it back. For the first time, sound can be stored.

events.title: Isandlwana
events.body: A Zulu army of about 20,000 overwhelms a British camp below Isandlwana hill, killing more than 1,300 soldiers — Britain's worst defeat by an African army. Britain wins the war that year.

events.title: The War of the Pacific
events.body: Chilean troops occupy the Bolivian port of Antofagasta, starting a war with Bolivia and Peru over nitrate deposits. Bolivia loses its whole coastline.

events.title: Indians Arrive in Fiji
events.body: The ship Leonidas lands the first indentured labourers from India in Fiji. About 60,000 follow over the next forty years.

events.title: The Light Bulb
events.body: Edison's team keeps a carbon-filament lamp glowing for more than half a day. Joseph Swan in England has been working on the same idea; electric light is about to change how people live after dark.

events.title: A Doll's House
events.body: Ibsen's play premieres in Copenhagen. Its last moment — Nora walking out on her husband and children and slamming the door — scandalises audiences across Europe.

events.title: France Digs at Panama
events.body: Ferdinand de Lesseps, builder of the Suez Canal, begins a canal across Panama. Yellow fever and malaria kill some 22,000 workers, by a common estimate, and the company collapses in 1889.

events.title: Geok Tepe
events.body: Russian troops under General Skobelev storm the Turkmen fortress of Geok Tepe and kill thousands, many of them civilians.

events.title: Majuba
events.body: Boer marksmen storm Majuba Hill and rout the British force on top, ending the First Anglo-Boer War. The Transvaal regains its independence under Paul Kruger.

events.title: The Tsar Assassinated
events.body: Revolutionaries of the People's Will kill Alexander II with a bomb in St Petersburg. His successor turns hard against reform.

events.title: Frozen Meat Crosses the World
events.body: The refrigerated ship Dunedin sails from New Zealand with frozen lamb and mutton, which arrives in London in good condition three months later.

events.title: The Tuberculosis Germ
events.body: Robert Koch announces in Berlin that he has found the bacterium that causes tuberculosis, then the deadliest disease in Europe.

events.title: The Chinese Exclusion Act
events.body: The United States bans Chinese labourers from immigrating — the first US law to bar a group by nationality.

events.title: The First Power Station
events.body: Edison's Pearl Street Station starts supplying electricity to customers in lower Manhattan.

events.title: Britain Occupies Egypt
events.body: British forces defeat Ahmed Urabi's nationalist army at Tel el-Kebir. British troops stay in Egypt until 1956.

events.title: Krakatoa
events.body: The volcanic island explodes with a sound heard thousands of kilometres away. Tsunamis kill more than 36,000 people, and sunsets around the world glow red for months.

events.title: The Berlin Conference
events.body: European powers meet in Berlin to set rules for claiming Africa. No Africans are invited. Within thirty years almost the whole continent is under European rule.

events.title: The Fall of Khartoum
events.body: The Mahdi's forces storm Khartoum after a ten-month siege and kill General Gordon. A Mahdist state rules Sudan until 1898.

events.title: Huckleberry Finn
events.body: Mark Twain's novel of a runaway boy and an escaped enslaved man, Jim, on the Mississippi is published in the United States, after an earlier British edition.

events.title: The Congo Free State
events.body: King Leopold II of Belgium is granted the vast Congo as his own possession. To meet rubber quotas, his agents take hostages and cut off hands; the population falls by millions, though estimates vary widely.

events.title: The Rabies Vaccine
events.body: Louis Pasteur gives his experimental rabies vaccine to nine-year-old Joseph Meister, bitten by a rabid dog. The boy survives.

events.title: Mandalay Falls
events.body: British troops take Mandalay and send King Thibaw into exile in India. All of Burma becomes part of British India.

events.title: The Indian National Congress
events.body: Seventy-two delegates meet in Bombay to found the Indian National Congress. It later leads the movement for independence.

events.title: The Motor Car
events.body: Carl Benz patents his three-wheeled 'vehicle powered by a gas engine'. In 1888 his wife Bertha drives it about 100 kilometres to show it works.

events.title: The First World Chess Championship
events.body: Wilhelm Steinitz beats Johannes Zukertort in a match played in New York, St. Louis and New Orleans, to become the first official world chess champion.

events.title: The Haymarket Affair
events.body: At a Chicago rally for the eight-hour day, a bomb kills police officers and police fire into the crowd. Workers around the world later mark 1 May in memory.

events.title: Coca-Cola
events.body: Atlanta pharmacist John Pemberton sells the first glasses of his new drink at a soda fountain, as a tonic.

events.title: The Uganda Martyrs
events.body: Kabaka Mwanga II of Buganda has young Christian converts burned to death at Namugongo. 3 June is still a day of pilgrimage for hundreds of thousands.

events.title: Gold on the Witwatersrand
events.body: Gold is found on the ridge of the Witwatersrand. Johannesburg grows from a mining camp to a city within a decade, built on the labour of migrant Black miners.

events.title: Cuba Abolishes Slavery
events.body: Spain ends slavery in Cuba, leaving Brazil the last country in the Americas to abolish it.

events.title: The Statue of Liberty
events.body: France's gift to the United States, built by Bartholdi on an iron frame by Gustave Eiffel, is dedicated in New York harbour.

events.title: Esperanto
events.body: Eye doctor L. L. Zamenhof publishes a booklet in Warsaw introducing an easy, neutral language he hopes will help peoples understand each other.

events.title: Sherlock Holmes
events.body: Arthur Conan Doyle's detective first appears in A Study in Scarlet, in a Christmas annual.

events.title: Brazil Abolishes Slavery
events.body: Princess Isabel signs the 'Golden Law'. Brazil, which took more enslaved Africans than any other country, is the last in the Americas to end slavery.

events.title: You Press the Button
events.body: George Eastman sells the first Kodak camera, loaded with film for 100 pictures: 'You press the button, we do the rest.' Photography becomes something anyone can do.

events.title: Van Gogh's Sunflowers
events.body: In Arles, waiting for Gauguin to join him, Vincent van Gogh paints sunflowers in a vase to decorate his room.

events.title: The Meiji Constitution
events.body: Japan adopts East Asia's first written constitution, with an elected parliament, modelled partly on Germany's.

events.title: The Eiffel Tower
events.body: Gustave Eiffel climbs to the top of his tower for its inauguration, ahead of the Paris World's Fair. At about 300 metres it is the tallest structure in the world, and many Parisians hate it.

events.title: May Day
events.body: Socialist parties found the Second International in Paris and call for workers everywhere to demonstrate on 1 May for the eight-hour day.

events.title: Brazil Becomes a Republic
events.body: A year after slavery is abolished, army officers depose Emperor Pedro II. The royal family sails into exile.

events.title: The Gibson Girl
events.body: Charles Dana Gibson's drawings of tall, confident young women set the ideal of the 1890s: shirtwaists, skirts free enough to cycle in, hair piled high.

events.title: The Pioneer Column
events.body: Cecil Rhodes's British South Africa Company sends armed settlers into Mashonaland, where they raise the flag at Fort Salisbury, now Harare.

events.title: Wounded Knee
events.body: US soldiers kill some 250 or more Lakota men, women and children at Wounded Knee Creek in South Dakota.

events.title: The Tobacco Protest
events.body: After the shah grants a British company control of Iran's tobacco trade, Iranians stop smoking at the call of a leading cleric. The shah cancels the concession weeks later.

events.title: Basketball
events.body: To keep students busy indoors in a Massachusetts winter, James Naismith nails up two peach baskets and writes thirteen rules.

events.title: Hawaii's Queen Overthrown
events.body: American businessmen, backed by US Marines, overthrow Queen Liliʻuokalani. The United States annexes Hawaii in 1898.

events.title: Gandhi Thrown Off a Train
events.body: A young Indian lawyer with a first-class ticket is thrown off the train at Pietermaritzburg station because he is not white. Gandhi later calls that cold night a turning point.

events.title: The Scream
events.body: Edvard Munch paints a figure clutching its face under a blood-red sky, from his memory of feeling 'an infinite scream passing through nature'.

events.title: Vivekananda in Chicago
events.body: At the World's Parliament of Religions, Swami Vivekananda opens with 'Sisters and Brothers of America' and introduces many Americans to Hinduism and yoga.

events.title: Women Vote in New Zealand
events.body: New Zealand becomes the first self-governing country to give women the vote in national elections, after petitions led by Kate Sheppard.

events.title: Labor Day
events.body: Twelve years after the first Labor Day parade in New York, Congress makes the first Monday in September a federal holiday — in the middle of the Pullman railway strike.

events.title: The Hamidian Massacres
events.body: Between 1894 and 1896, Ottoman troops and irregulars kill Armenians across eastern Anatolia; estimates range from 100,000 to 300,000.

events.title: The First Sino-Japanese War
events.body: Japan defeats Qing China over control of Korea. In the 1895 peace treaty China gives up Taiwan.

events.title: The Glen Grey Act
events.body: Cecil Rhodes's Cape government limits African land holdings and taxes men who do not work for wages — a model for later segregation laws.

events.title: The Dreyfus Affair
events.body: Jewish army captain Alfred Dreyfus is wrongly convicted of spying for Germany and sent to Devil's Island. The case splits France for a decade.

events.title: The Importance of Being Earnest
events.body: Oscar Wilde's comedy opens in London. Within months he is on trial and jailed for gross indecency, and his name is taken off the posters.

events.title: José Martí Falls
events.body: The poet and exiled leader of Cuban independence is killed in one of the first battles of the new war against Spain.

events.title: Queen Min Assassinated
events.body: Japanese agents break into Seoul's Gyeongbok Palace and kill Korea's Queen Min, who had resisted Japanese influence.

events.title: X-Rays
events.body: Wilhelm Röntgen notices a screen glowing across his darkened lab in Würzburg. Within weeks his image of his wife's hand bones astonishes the world.

events.title: The First Film Show
events.body: The Lumière brothers show ten short films to a paying audience in a Paris café. Cinema is born.

events.title: The Jameson Raid
events.body: Leander Starr Jameson leads about 600 armed men into the Transvaal, hoping to spark a rising against Kruger's government. They surrender within days; Rhodes resigns as Cape prime minister.

events.title: Adwa
events.body: Emperor Menelik II and Empress Taytu's armies crush an Italian invasion. Ethiopia stays independent, and the victory becomes a symbol for Africans everywhere.

events.title: Radioactivity
events.body: Henri Becquerel finds that uranium salts fog a photographic plate in the dark — the first sign of radioactivity.

events.title: The First Chimurenga
events.body: The Ndebele and then the Shona rise against the British South Africa Company. The spirit medium Nehanda is hanged in 1898; words attributed to her, 'my bones will rise again', inspire later liberation fighters.

events.title: The First Modern Olympics
events.body: About 240 athletes, all men, from 14 nations compete in Athens. Spyridon Louis, a water carrier, wins the first marathon for Greece.

events.title: Plessy v. Ferguson
events.body: The US Supreme Court rules that racially segregated facilities are lawful if 'separate but equal'.

events.title: Rinderpest
events.body: A cattle plague sweeps through southern Africa, killing most of the cattle — and much wildlife — on which herding peoples depend.

events.title: The Greenhouse Effect Calculated
events.body: Svante Arrhenius calculates how much the Earth would warm if the carbon dioxide in the air doubled — the first calculation of how carbon dioxide warms the planet.

events.title: Ludo
events.body: A simplified version of the Indian game pachisi is patented in England as Ludo.

events.title: Plague in Bombay
events.body: Bubonic plague reaches Bombay. Over the following decades it kills millions in India.

events.title: José Rizal Executed
events.body: The novelist whose Noli Me Tángere exposed Spanish colonial abuses is shot by a firing squad in Manila. He becomes the Philippines' national hero.

events.title: The Benin Expedition
events.body: A British force sacks Benin City and carries off thousands of bronzes and ivories, now spread through museums worldwide. Campaigns for their return continue.

events.title: Dracula
events.body: Bram Stoker's novel of the Transylvanian count who comes to London is published.

events.title: Nkosi Sikelel' iAfrika
events.body: Enoch Sontonga, a teacher and choirmaster, composes a hymn, 'God Bless Africa'. It becomes the anthem of the liberation movement and part of South Africa's national anthem.

events.title: The First Zionist Congress
events.body: Theodor Herzl gathers Zionist delegates in Basel, who call for a Jewish homeland in Palestine.

events.title: Canudos
events.body: After a year of war, the Brazilian army destroys Canudos, a backlands community of poor followers of the preacher Antônio Conselheiro. Most of its people are killed.

events.title: J'Accuse…!
events.body: Émile Zola's open letter on the front page of a Paris newspaper accuses the army of covering up Dreyfus's innocence. Zola is convicted of libel and flees to England.

events.title: The Spanish–American War
events.body: The US battleship Maine explodes in Havana harbour. In the war that follows, the United States takes Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines from Spain, and Cuba gains independence under US influence.

events.title: The First Philippine Republic
events.body: Emilio Aguinaldo declares the Philippines independent from Spain. The United States annexes the islands instead, and in the Philippine–American War of 1899–1902 hundreds of thousands of Filipinos die.

events.title: Omdurman
events.body: British and Egyptian forces with machine guns kill around 10,000 Sudanese soldiers in a morning, for a few dozen of their own dead.

events.title: The Hundred Days' Reform Ends
events.body: The Guangxu Emperor's rush of modernising reforms is ended by a coup of the Empress Dowager Cixi. The emperor is confined and six reformers are executed.

events.title: Samori Touré Captured
events.body: After sixteen years of resisting the French, Samori Touré is captured and exiled to Gabon, where he dies in 1900.

events.title: The Seagull Reborn
events.body: Chekhov's play, a disaster in St Petersburg two years earlier, triumphs at the new Moscow Art Theatre under Stanislavski. The theatre takes a seagull as its emblem.

events.title: Radium
events.body: Marie and Pierre Curie announce a second new radioactive element, radium, after polonium earlier that year.

events.title: Heart of Darkness
events.body: Joseph Conrad's novella of a voyage up an African river, drawn from his own journey on the Congo in 1890, begins appearing in a magazine.

events.title: Aspirin
events.body: Bayer registers the name Aspirin for its acetylsalicylic acid, a pain reliever related to a remedy from willow bark.

events.title: Maple Leaf Rag
events.body: Scott Joplin's piano rag is published in Sedalia, Missouri. It sells widely and makes ragtime a craze — a root of jazz.

events.title: The Famine of 1899–1900
events.body: Failed monsoon rains bring famine to western and central India. Estimates of the dead range from about one million to several million.

events.title: The South African War Begins
events.body: War breaks out between Britain and the two Boer republics over the gold-rich Transvaal. Black South Africans fight and die on both sides, and in the camps.

events.title: The Natal Indian Ambulance Corps
events.body: Gandhi organises over a thousand Indian volunteers in Natal as stretcher-bearers for the British in the South African War.
